pricing.refundBody: Try the pack with your own numbers. If it isn’t right for you, email us within 30 days for a full refund.

items.a: Open the seven-day Quick Start Guide first. It points you toward the first tasks, then the workbook and twelve-chapter reading path.

items.q: Is the pack useful if I have debt?
items.a: Debt decisions are part of the book, including Tanya’s composite story. The material is educational and does not replace advice about your individual circumstances.

items.q: Do I need Excel or paid software?
items.a: The workbook is designed for Excel and free Google Sheets. You can print the checklists and keep using the downloadable resources.

items.q: What if my income or situation is different?
items.a: The pack includes sections for tight budgets, higher earners, couples and families, readers 50 and over, and irregular income. The calculators use your own numbers.

items.q: What is different from watching the channel?
items.a: The pack gives you an ordered twelve-chapter path, editable calculators, reusable checklists and scripts in one place. You can return to the tools while working with your own numbers.
At launch, the pack will be available as a download after checkout, with an email containing your access links. Purchases are not enabled in this preview.

items.q: What if it is not right for me?
items.a: The planned offer includes a full refund within 30 days. The final support address and refund process will be shown before purchases are enabled.

examples.title: Put recurring costs in one place.
examples.intro: Start with three costs you recognize. You do not have to make every decision today.
steps: Write down the cost and how often you pay it.
Multiply monthly costs by 12, weekly costs by 52, and yearly costs by 1.
Mark each one: keep, review, or unsure.
Choose one cost to investigate. Check the terms before making a change.
examples.footer: A clear list comes before a decision.

examples.title: Ask a clearer question about a bill.
examples.intro: A simple starting point for a conversation with a service provider.
examples.quote: Hello. I am reviewing my recurring bills. Could you explain my current plan, any extra fees and the lower-cost options available? Before I change anything, please confirm the total price, what I would lose and whether there is a contract or cancellation fee.
steps: Have the current bill beside you.
Write down the total offered price and any conditions.
Ask for the details in writing before deciding.
examples.footer: A question starts the conversation. It does not guarantee a discount.
